result.conclusion: Object shape does NOT beat category head-to-head, but it comes close and is the more mechanistic signal: held-out category-only AUC 0.661 vs nonlinear-shape-only 0.645 (category wins by +0.016 in 96% of 120 run-split CVs), while shape explains 53% of per-category SR variance and — critically — WITHIN-category height variation predicts failure with the same per-meter logit slope as between-category (−5.6 vs −7.1 logit/m, cell-perm p<0.003), so shape is causal-ish rather than a mere category proxy; category identity carries only a modest residual (+0.008 AUC on top of shape when combined). The shape effect is entirely a grasp-phase phenomenon (grasp AUC 0.633 vs transport/place 0.509, null) and is non-monotonic: SR peaks at height 0.04–0.08 m and ramps down from ~0.08–0.10 m (no sharp cliff; best single threshold h>0.212 m costs −0.22 SR out-of-sample). Caveat: eval configs repeat across runs, so held-out-run CV is not fully independent (affects both models; category possibly favored via repeated instances), and the transport/place null is underpowered below AUC~0.55.

result.conclusion: Start location is a real, checkpoint-robust driver of success, but the geometry is radial, not directional: there is no near/far gradient (far-near = -0.014, p=0.36) and no left/right gradient (p=0.15); instead placements on the outer rim of the counter placement region (max(|x_rel|,|y_rel|)>0.65, 26% of episodes) lose 18.3 SR points (0.330 vs 0.513 run-adjusted, perm p=1e-4, negative in 27/28 runs), producing a bull's-eye heatmap (corner cells 0.25-0.35 vs central cells 0.55-0.66). Absolute kitchen coordinates add nothing beyond region-relative position (dR2<=0.0006), rim failures occur by the same no-grasp mechanism as elsewhere (phase mix flat across regions), and rim placement is uncorrelated with category or object size, so location and shape are additive orthogonal factors of similar magnitude (R2 0.041 vs 0.052, together 0.095). For data prescription this means targeting the rim of the placement region is a cleaner location-based weak-region signal than any compass direction; caveat: rows repeat eval configs across runs (3154 unique of 7112), mitigated by within-run stratification and the 27/28-run sign consistency.

Caveat: paired eval configs repeat across runs, which demonstrably inflated the naive layout effect; all headline numbers use run-demeaned, within-run-permutation, and multi-factor-controlled estimates.

result.conclusion: Category signal is real and large, not noise: the spread of per-category (run-demeaned) success rates is 2.4x what a within-run label-permutation null produces (SD 0.155 vs 0.063, p=0.0005; implied true signal SD 0.141, i.e. 83% of observed spread variance is genuine), and per-category SRs replicate across disjoint run halves (r=0.73) and disjoint eval configs (r=0.66). The user "cannot find a pattern" for two reasons: (a) individual category estimates carry ±12pp Wilson-CI noise at median n=58 so mid-table ordering is unreadable, and (b) only ~43% of the category variance is explained by measured shape (and 53% by all of shape+location+layout+style), so no simple geometric rule is visible by eye — the remaining ~half is category-idiosyncratic (grasp affordance: hardest = kettle_non_electric, blender_jug, saucepan_lid, water_bottle, teapot; easiest = canned_food, cucumber, corn, potato, tangerine). In a run-CV ridge decomposition, category is the single strongest family (alone R²=0.073, within-run AUC 0.66) and retains the largest added-last increment (+0.028 R², +0.026 AUC, residual perm p=0.0005), so category should be kept as a targeting variable rather than replaced by shape features; caveat: eval configs repeat across runs (1194 configs in >1 run) so cross-run rows are correlated, which the config-split reliability check explicitly controls for.

answers.question: (1) How to pin kitchen layout and style (layout_ids/style_ids or equivalent); where consumed; accepted values; how the user's eval scripts currently set them
answers.answer: Kitchen.__init__ accepts three kwargs: layout_and_style_ids, layout_ids, style_ids (kitchen.py:392-394). If layout_and_style_ids is given it must be a list of [layout,style] pairs (or strings '5x5'/'5x1'); otherwise layout_ids x style_ids are cross-producted (kitchen.py:424-438), then filtered by class EXCLUDE_LAYOUTS/EXCLUDE_STYLES (kitchen.py:441-445; both empty for PickPlaceCounterToSink, which defines no override — base defaults at kitchen.py:212-214). Per reset, ONE pair is drawn with env.rng from that list (kitchen.py:595) unless ep_meta already contains layout_id/style_id (kitchen.py:591-593), and is passed to KitchenArena (kitchen.py:611-618). Accepted values: ints 1-60 (LayoutType/StyleType enums, scene_registry.py:9-100+) or negative group ids: -1=test(1-10), -2=train(11-60), -3=all(1-60), plus layout-only -4/-5/-6 (LAYOUT_GROUPS_TO_IDS scene_registry.py:85-92, STYLE_GROUPS_TO_IDS:166-170, unpack fns:239-276). So pinning = layout_and_style_ids=[[11,11]] (single pair -> rng.choice is a no-op) or layout_ids=11, style_ids=11. CRITICAL: create_env's split kwarg OVERRIDES these — split='pretrain' forces layout_ids=-2, style_ids=-2 (env_utils.py:86-104); you must pass split=None to have your ids respected. Current user scripts do NOT pin: rollout_eval.py:63-70 calls create_env(split=args.split) with default 'pretrain' (rollout_eval.py:173) -> random layout/style 11-60 every reset; build_eval_set.py:26-30 passes layout_ids=-2, style_ids=-2 explicitly (2500 combos, seed-determined); capture_rollouts.py:24 and record_pi0_demos.py:119 use gym.make(..., split='pretrain'). Verified empirically: with layout_and_style_ids=[[11,11]] all 5 seeds produced layout=11, style=11.

answers.question: (2) How object start placement is sampled for PickPlaceCounterToSink; can it be pinned to fixed XY / narrow region; minimal mechanism
answers.answer: The target object's placement is hardcoded in PickPlaceCounterToSink._get_obj_cfgs (kitchen_pick_place.py:294-318): placement=dict(fixture=self.counter, sample_region_kwargs=dict(ref=self.sink, loc='left_right'), size=(0.30,0.40), pos=('ref',-1.0)). Consumption chain: EnvUtils._get_placement_initializer (env_utils.py:906, called from kitchen.py:804) -> counter.sample_reset_region (env_utils.py:1080) which rng.choice's among valid counter-top regions (fixture.py:383) — loc='left_right' yields up to TWO candidate regions (left/right of sink, counter.py:595-790), i.e. a per-episode coin flip; then an inner region of placement['size'] is positioned via pos within the outer region (env_utils.py:1099-1256) and the final XY is drawn uniformly by UniformRandomSampler._sample_x/_sample_y (placement_samplers.py:225-266); yaw drawn from default rotation=(-pi/4,pi/4) (env_utils.py:992). There is NO env kwarg exposing placement; minimal-invasive mechanism = monkeypatch the class method before env creation (verified working): wrap _get_obj_cfgs and for the cfg named 'obj' set sample_region_kwargs['loc']='left' (kills the coin flip), size=(0.02,0.02) (or (0.0,0.0) for an exact point), ensure_object_boundary_in_range=False (else the degenerate range raises PlacementError, placement_samplers.py:239-243; flag read at env_utils.py:1002-1004), rotation=0.0 (pins yaw). Measured result: object XY spread 1.9cm x 1.7cm over 5 seeds (residual comes from the 2cm region + the 10-step settle loop at kitchen.py:1146). Equivalent alternative: subclass PickPlaceCounterToSink overriding _get_obj_cfgs — robosuite's EnvMeta auto-registers it, robosuite.make('YourSubclass') works. A third path pins the REGION but not exact XY: env.set_ep_meta(saved_meta) before reset — cfg['reset_region'] is reused verbatim (env_utils.py:1069-1070). Also zero the robot spawn jitter: robot_spawn_deviation_pos_x/pos_y/rot default 0.15/0.05/0.0 (kitchen.py:405-407,415-417) — pass 0.0 to pin the base (verified identical base across seeds).

answers.question: (3) Is the sink (goal) position fully determined by the layout?
answers.answer: Yes. The task registers the sink as a fixture reference (kitchen_pick_place.py:272-275, register_fixture_ref(FixtureType.SINK)) and success = object inside that sink (kitchen_pick_place.py:352-362). The sink is a built-in fixture embedded in a counter at fixed fractional coordinates in the layout blueprint yaml (e.g. layout011.yaml:389-396: 'interior_obj: sink, obj_x_percent: 0.52'), instantiated by KitchenArena(layout_id,...) (kitchen.py:611-618); it has no sampled placement (only accessory fixtures go through the fixture-placement sampling in kitchen.py:663-790). All 60 layout yamls (50 train + 10 test) contain a sink, so no layout lacks the goal. Verified empirically: env.get_fixture('sink').pos identical (0.300,-1.796) across 5 different seeds at layout_and_style_ids=[[11,11]]. Pinning the layout therefore pins the goal exactly.

answers.question: (4) How object category/instance is chosen per episode; what the reset seed controls; can you sweep only the object; deterministic-reset path
answers.answer: Category/instance: the 'obj' cfg uses obj_groups (an ENV KWARG — PickPlace.__init__ kitchen_pick_place.py:14-18, default 'all') filtered by graspable=True, washable=True (kitchen_pick_place.py:306-307). create_obj (env_utils.py:1403-1491) -> sample_kitchen_object_helper: category = rng.choice(valid_categories) (kitchen_object_utils.py:440), registry weighted-choice (:463-467), instance = rng.choice(mjcf_paths) (:469), with obj_instance_split 'pretrain'/'target' filtering instances (:451-461). Passing obj_groups='<abs path to model.xml>' selects an EXACT instance deterministically (kitchen_object_utils.py:361-382). Seed: robosuite base MujocoEnv sets self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) ONCE at construction (robosuite/environments/base.py:144-145); every stochastic step (layout choice kitchen.py:595, region choice fixture.py:383, XY/yaw placement_samplers.py, category/instance choice, robot-base jitter) consumes this single stream, so episode k after construction is a deterministic function of (seed, kwargs, k). Deterministic paths: (a) fresh env per seed (build_eval_set.py:23-31 pattern — 1 env = 1 episode = pure function of seed); (b) gym wrapper reset(seed=k) RE-SEEDS env.rng before every reset (gym_wrapper.py:342-344) — same effect without env re-creation; (c) exact replay: env.set_ep_meta(meta) then reset() (robosuite base.py:404-410) pins layout/style (kitchen.py:591-593), exact object instances via stored info.mjcf_path (kitchen.py:854-861 + env_utils.py:1413-1426), reset_region (env_utils.py:1069-1070) and robot base pos (kitchen.py:1118-1121) — everything except the exact XY draw within the region. Object-only sweep: verified — with layout/style pinned, placement monkeypatched and obj_groups='cup', 5 seeds gave identical kitchen/sink/base, XY within 2cm, instances varying (cup_4,cup_3,...). For exact control, enumerate instances via obj_groups=xml-path with a fixed seed instead of sweeping seeds. Caveat: obj_groups categories must satisfy graspable+washable or valid_categories is empty and rng.choice throws.

answers.question: (5) Where these knobs go in the data-GENERATION pipeline (mimicgen configs, pi0/GR00T collection scripts) for a fixed-context training set
answers.answer: Three insertion points. (i) Expert rollout collection: transfer/new_files/record_pi0_demos.py:119 builds the env via gym.make(f'robocasa/{task}', split=args.split, seed=...). The gym wrapper forwards **kwargs -> create_env -> robosuite.make -> Kitchen (gym_wrapper.py:169-177, env_utils.py:112-137), so change that call to gym.make(..., split=None, obj_instance_split='pretrain', layout_and_style_ids=[[11,11]], obj_groups=<category or xml path>, robot_spawn_deviation_pos_x=0.0, robot_spawn_deviation_pos_y=0.0, robot_spawn_deviation_rot=0.0, seed=...) and import the _get_obj_cfgs monkeypatch module at the top of the script (it must run in-process; it is NOT stored in the hdf5). Same one-line change applies to capture_rollouts.py:24 and to build_eval_set.py:26-30 / rollout_eval.py:63-70 on the eval side. (ii) The hdf5 env_args: build_env_info (record_pi0_demos.py:34-51) is the config that convert_to_robomimic_format writes into data.attrs['env_args'] (robomimic_dataset_utils.py:274-291); add the same kwargs (layout_and_style_ids, obj_groups, obj_instance_split, robot_spawn_deviation_*) into that dict — this is what any downstream env-recreation uses. (iii) mimicgen generation: /data/xinyua11/mimicgen/mimicgen/scripts/generate_dataset.py:143 reads env_meta from the SOURCE hdf5 (env_args) and data_generator.py:246 calls env.reset() per NEW generated episode — so once (ii) is done, mimicgen-generated episodes are fixed-context too (but the placement monkeypatch must also be importable/applied in the mimicgen process, e.g. via a small sitecustomize-style import or by using a registered subclass whose name is stored as env_name). The LeRobot conversion (robocasa/scripts/dataset_scripts/convert_hdf5_lerobot.py:79,99) replays EXACT stored mujoco states via env.reset_to (robomimic_env_wrapper.py:153-183 uses set_ep_meta + model xml), so it inherits fixed context automatically with no changes. Note /data/xinyua11/robocasa/mimicgen_src is the DATA directory (source hdf5s, generated/, lerobot/); the mimicgen code lives at /data/xinyua11/mimicgen.

answers.question: (6) Gotchas: placement feasibility, layouts lacking sink, distribution shift, fork quirks
answers.answer: (a) split kwarg silently overrides your layout pins (env_utils.py:86-104) — always pass split=None and set obj_instance_split yourself. (b) The gym wrapper's DEFAULT split='test' (gym_wrapper.py:151) is not a valid create_env value and raises ValueError — always pass split explicitly. (c) Degenerate placement size with the default ensure_object_boundary_in_range=True raises PlacementError (placement_samplers.py:239-243) — set ensure_object_boundary_in_range=False when size < object footprint; also a 4cm margin is subtracted from the outer region (env_utils.py:1105-1108). (d) loc='left_right' is a hidden per-episode coin flip between two counter regions (fixture.py:383) — pin loc='left' or 'right'; note left/right feasibility varies per layout, and PlacementError triggers up to 50 full _load_model retries (kitchen.py:647-650) then RuntimeError — if a chosen layout's left region is too small for tall objects, switch side or enlarge size slightly. (e) The distractor objects (distr_counter on the counter at offset (0,0.30), distr_sink inside the sink; kitchen_pick_place.py:321-348) are sampled from obj_groups='all' every episode — for strict object-only variation pin their categories (or drop them) in the same monkeypatch, and beware a huge distractor colliding with a tightly pinned target region. (f) Yaw is random +/-45 deg by default (env_utils.py:992) — set placement['rotation']=0.0. (g) Exact XY repeatability is ~1-2cm, not exact, due to the uniform draw inside even a 2cm region plus the 10-step physics settle (kitchen.py:1146); bitwise-identical starts require state replay (reset_to). (h) No sink-less layouts: all 60 layouts contain a sink and PickPlaceCounterToSink has no EXCLUDE_LAYOUTS, but layouts 1-10 are the TEST split (scene_registry.py:197-199) — use a layout/style in 11-60 for training data to preserve the project's train/test convention. (i) Fresh-env-per-seed is what makes seed->episode a pure function; reusing one env and calling reset() repeatedly advances the rng stream (robosuite base.py:145 seeds only at construction) — use gym reset(seed=k) (gym_wrapper.py:342-344) or set_ep_meta for reuse. (j) Fork quirks: obj_registries defaults to ('objaverse','lightwheel') (kitchen.py:397-400) unlike upstream ('objaverse','aai'), so instance counts/paths differ from upstream docs; robots renamed PandaMobile->PandaOmron (kitchen.py:460-463); hard_reset=True is forced (kitchen.py:521) so every reset rebuilds the model (pinning cost: ~10-20s/reset CPU). (k) Train-eval distribution shift: a policy trained only on one (layout,style) will look better on the matching fixed-context eval and WORSE on the existing split='pretrain' eval sets (phase1_data/eval_set.json seeds encode mixed layouts) — results are not comparable to prior arms (core/random/coverage were trained+evaled under layout variation); report the fixed-context arm on BOTH the fixed-context eval and the standard pretrain eval, and keep eval seeds (<1000) disjoint from generation seeds (>=1000 or 100000+ as record_pi0_demos already does).

SHARED STEP 0 — one small module, used by both eval and generation. Create /data/xinyua11/robocasa/policy_analysis/fixed_context.py:

  import numpy as np
  from robocasa.environments.kitchen.atomic.kitchen_pick_place import PickPlaceCounterToSink
  FIXED_LAYOUT_STYLE = [[11, 11]]          # any (l,s) with l,s in 11..60; keep constant everywhere
  _orig = PickPlaceCounterToSink._get_obj_cfgs
  def _pinned(self):
      cfgs = _orig(self)
      for cfg in cfgs:
          p = cfg["placement"]
          if cfg["name"] == "obj":
              p["sample_region_kwargs"]["loc"] = "left"        # kill left/right coin flip
              p["size"] = (0.02, 0.02)                          # ~point region ((0.0,0.0) for exact center)
              p["pos"] = ("ref", -1.0)
              p["ensure_object_boundary_in_range"] = False      # required for tiny regions
              p["rotation"] = 0.0                               # pin yaw
          elif cfg["name"] == "distr_counter":
              cfg["obj_groups"] = "bowl"                        # pin distractor identity (or leave; must match train/eval)
          elif cfg["name"] == "distr_sink":
              cfg["obj_groups"] = "sponge"
      return cfgs
  PickPlaceCounterToSink._get_obj_cfgs = _pinned
  FIXED_ENV_KWARGS = dict(
      split=None,                                              # REQUIRED: split overrides layout ids (env_utils.py:86-104)
      obj_instance_split="pretrain",                           # keep instance-level train/test disjointness ("target"/None for eval variants)
      layout_and_style_ids=FIXED_LAYOUT_STYLE,
      robot_spawn_deviation_pos_x=0.0, robot_spawn_deviation_pos_y=0.0, robot_spawn_deviation_rot=0.0,
  )

(a) FIXED-CONTEXT EVAL SET
1. Enumerate the object sweep. Category sweep: pick washable+graspable categories (e.g. cup, mug, bowl...). Instance sweep (fully deterministic): per category, list instance xmls via `from robocasa.models.objects.kitchen_objects import OBJ_CATEGORIES; OBJ_CATEGORIES["cup"]["objaverse"].mjcf_paths` and pass one path as obj_groups (kitchen_object_utils.py:361-382 spawns exactly that instance).
2. Build the eval manifest (adapt build_eval_set.py:23-31): for each (object_spec, seed) pair create a FRESH env — `import fixed_context; env = robosuite.make(env_name="PickPlaceCounterToSink", robots="PandaOmron", controller_configs=cc, has_renderer=False, has_offscreen_renderer=False, use_camera_obs=False, use_object_obs=True, ignore_done=True, seed=seed, obj_groups=object_spec, **fixed_context.FIXED_ENV_KWARGS)`; env.reset(); save `env.get_ep_meta()` (JSON) per episode into eval_fixed_context.json. Use eval seeds < 1000 (project convention). ~10 seeds x N objects, or 1 fixed seed x all instances for a pure object sweep.
3. Run policy eval (adapt rollout_eval.py:63-70): either (i) rebuild with the same kwargs+seed per episode (create_env forwards **kwargs: pass seed=..., obj_groups=..., **FIXED_ENV_KWARGS with camera_names/widths as now), or (ii) exact-replay: one env, per episode `env.set_ep_meta(saved_meta); env.reset()` (robosuite base.py:404; pins layout/style/instance/region/base — only the <=2cm XY draw re-samples). For gym-based eval (pi0/GR00T servers, as in analyze_pi0_weakregions): `env = gym.make("robocasa/PickPlaceCounterToSink", seed=seed, obj_groups=..., **FIXED_ENV_KWARGS)` then `env.reset()`; or reuse one env and call `env.reset(seed=k)` which re-seeds env.rng (gym_wrapper.py:342-344).
4. Sanity-check the manifest: assert a single (layout_id,style_id), sink pos constant, obj_xy spread < 3cm, and that only info.cat / info.mjcf_path vary across episodes.

(b) FIXED-CONTEXT TRAINING DATA GENERATION
1. Patch record_pi0_demos.py (the runnable copy under robocasa_experiments; source at transfer/new_files/record_pi0_demos.py): add `import fixed_context` at the top (after robocasa import), and change line 119 to `env = gym.make(f"robocasa/{args.task}", seed=args.seed + attempts, obj_groups=args.obj_groups, **fixed_context.FIXED_ENV_KWARGS)` (add an --obj_groups arg; keep generation seeds >= 100000, disjoint from eval). Drop the height-band rejection flags if the object set is now explicit.
2. Also add the same kwargs into build_env_info's config dict (record_pi0_demos.py:38-50): `"layout_and_style_ids": [[11,11]], "obj_instance_split": "pretrain", "robot_spawn_deviation_pos_x": 0.0, "robot_spawn_deviation_pos_y": 0.0, "robot_spawn_deviation_rot": 0.0` (obj_groups too if fixed for the whole file). convert_to_robomimic_format copies this into data.attrs["env_args"] (robomimic_dataset_utils.py:274-291) so every downstream env recreation is fixed-context.
3. Collect: run with the pi0 (or GR00T) server up, sweeping obj_groups across your object list, e.g. `--n_success 10` per object -> one hdf5 (or one per object, then merge). Successful demos store model_file + ep_meta + full mujoco states (record_pi0_demos.py:140-142,193-196).
4. Convert to LeRobot exactly as before: `python robocasa/scripts/dataset_scripts/convert_hdf5_lerobot.py --raw_dataset_path <hdf5> --camera_names robot0_agentview_left robot0_agentview_right robot0_eye_in_hand --camera_height 256 --camera_width 256` — it replays exact states via reset_to (convert_hdf5_lerobot.py:79,99), so fixed context is inherited with no changes.
5. (Optional mimicgen amplification): mimicgen's generate_dataset.py reads env_args from the source hdf5 (line 143) and resets the env per generated episode (data_generator.py:246), so step 2 pins its context — BUT the placement monkeypatch is code, not config: make sure `import fixed_context` runs in the mimicgen process too (wrap generate_dataset in a small launcher that imports it first). If you want the pinning to survive env_args round-trips without an import, instead define `class PPC2SinkFixed(PickPlaceCounterToSink)` overriding _get_obj_cfgs in an installed module (robosuite auto-registers subclasses) and use env_name="PPC2SinkFixed" everywhere, including build_env_info.
6. Train the DP/pi0 arm on the resulting LeRobot set as usual (ppc2sink_pi0.yaml pattern), and evaluate on BOTH the fixed-context eval set from (a) (matched context: isolates object effect) and the existing split='pretrain' eval seeds (measures the single-kitchen distribution-shift penalty).

Results from fixed-context training/eval are not directly comparable to the project's earlier arms (those trained and evaluated under layout/style variation with split='pretrain'); keep the standard eval alongside.
